evidence.quote:
It was the Yuletide, which men call Christmas, though they know in
their hearts it is older than Bethlehem and Babylon, older than
Memphis and mankind.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator frames the festival as predating all recorded human history.

evidence.quote:
where also they had
commanded their sons to keep festival once every century, that the
memory of primal secrets might not be forgotten
evidence.paraphrase: A hereditary rite must be kept once per century to preserve ancient secrets.

evidence.quote:
Finally I was sure it was not a face at all, but a
fiendishly cunning mask. The eyes never moved, and the skin was too
like wax.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator becomes convinced the old man's face is a waxen mask.

evidence.quote:
the unmentionable "Necronomicon" of the mad Arab Abdul Alhazred, in
Olaus Wormius
cent Latin translation: a book which I had never
seen, but of which I had heard monstrous things whispered
evidence.paraphrase: A forbidden book of monstrous lore is introduced among the old volumes.

evidence.quote:
After more eons of descent I saw some side
passages or burrows leading from unknown recesses of blackness to
this shaft of nighted mystery.
evidence.paraphrase: A seemingly endless descent leads deep beneath the town into unknown passages.

evidence.quote:
suddenly there spread out before me
the boundless vista of an inner world
cent a vast fungous shore litten
by a belching column of sick greenish flame and washed by a wide
oily river that flowed from abysses frightful and unsuspected
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator discovers a vast subterranean inner world with a glowing flame and river.

evidence.quote:
But what frightened me most was that flaming column; spouting
volcanically from depths profound and inconceivable, casting no
shadows as healthy flame should
evidence.paraphrase: The flame is described as anomalous because, unlike normal fire, it casts no shadows and has no warmth.

evidence.quote:
there flopped
rhythmically a horde of tame, trained, hybrid winged things that no
sound eye could ever wholly grasp, or sound brain ever wholly
remember
evidence.paraphrase: A horde of unnatural hybrid winged creatures emerges and is ridden by the celebrants.

evidence.quote:
But it was a hideous proof, because
I knew from old papers that that watch had been buried with my
great-great-great-great-grandfather in 1698.
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator recognizes the offered watch as one buried with a long-dead ancestor, deepening his horror.

evidence.quote:
the
suddenness of his motion dislodged the waxen mask from what should
have been his head. And then, because that nightmare
cent s position
barred me from the stone staircase down which we had come, I flung

evidence.paraphrase: The mask is dislodged to reveal something monstrous, and the narrator flings himself into the underground river to escape.

evidence.quote:
Everything was
wrong, with the broad window showing a sea of roofs in which only
about one in five was ancient, and the sound of trolleys and motors
in the streets below.
evidence.paraphrase: Waking in the hospital, the narrator finds a modern Kingsport of trolleys and motors, contrasting with the ancient town he experienced.

evidence.quote:
They told me I had taken the wrong fork of
the hill road the night before, and fallen over the cliffs at Orange
Point
cent a thing they deducted from prints found in the snow.
evidence.paraphrase: Authorities reconstruct the narrator's accident by deducing his path from footprints in the snow.

evidence.quote:
So I read again that hideous chapter, and shuddered doubly because
it was indeed not new to me. I had seen it before, let footprints
tell what they might
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator insists the experience was real despite evidence, having encountered the book's text before.
A quoted passage from the Necronomicon offers a pseudo-explanation of how horrid life arises from corruption of the dead.
